commits.message: test(markup): name the tickets that own the pinned divergences

fix(markup): take the reference's tag grammar, not a redrawing of it (rich-markup-sec)

`TAG_RE` carried a hand-written character class where `rich/markup.py` has
`RE_TAGS`, and the two had drifted in both directions at once. It invented
uppercase, so `[INFO] starting up` was taken as an opening tag and printed as
` starting up` — silent text loss on every `Console.print`, since `markup.render`
is the path every string takes. And it omitted `@` plus every punctuation
character the reference admits, so `[a+b]` stayed literal where Rich styles it.

Replace the enumeration with the reference's own expression rather than a
re-derivation of it, so the two can be read side by side.

Two consequences of the narrowed opening class:

- `[/ ]` now reaches the parser. The reference strips the name before asking
  whether one is left, making that an implicit close; testing the raw tag text
  against the literal `"/"` answered a narrower question and would have made it
  an explicit close of the empty style. Derive the discriminator from the name.

- `MarkupRegistry.register` promised to reject names markup can never address,
  but its class opened on `[A-Za-z]`. Nothing lowercases a tag on the way in, so
  `register("Foo", ...)` would now install a handler that could never fire.
  Narrow it to `[a-z]` and pin it.

`markup-grammar.golden.txt` is generated by Python Rich and pins both directions
— which brackets become tags and which stay literal — end to end through
`Console.print` with colour forced on, because the two ports differ in how they
carry an unresolvable style name on a span while printing identical bytes. The
suite could not have caught any of this before: narrowing the class to `[a-z#]`
passed all 2259 tests unchanged.

Three divergences found while building the corpus are pinned as their own checks
with the reference's answer beside ours, rather than folded in: a nested colour
override is dropped (spans are applied in close order, not by start), a combined
style emits its SGR parameters colour-first, and a doubled backslash before a
tag is not halved.

docs(text): point the full-justify note at the ticket that owns it (#99)

`rich-justify-0cr.1` already tracked implementing full justification, with
three siblings covering the table, the docs, and the skipped expand test.
The note added with the justify fixture cited a new ticket filed without
checking, which is a second entry for one fact.
